title: Dedicated autoscaler: throughput guarantees, burst control improvements, and utilization reporting
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers running Dedicated fleets reported intermittent latency spikes during short bursty traffic (minute-scale) while still needing strict throughput guarantees for steady-state jobs. The autoscaler previously prioritized pod counts for average utilization targets, which allowed short bursts to exhaust token buckets and trigger temporary throttling. Motivation: provide deterministic throughput guarantees for high-priority routes while preserving burst allowance for latency-sensitive requests and improving utilization reporting so SRE/product can tune policies. This PR implements: 1) throughput_guarantee policy: allows allocation of reserved throughput (requests/sec and tokens/sec) per priority class with hard enforcement in the autoscaler and admission layer; 2) burst control refactor: token-bucket-based burst allowance moved into the autoscaler core with smoother decay and per-fleet configurable smoothing window; 3) utilization reporting: per-fleet and per-priority time-series (1s/10s/1m) and p99 queueing latency metrics exported to metrics backend and tied into Console dashboards; 4) rollout-safe changes: feature flag (autoscaler.throughput_guarantee.enabled) and gradual rollout via canary percent for Dedicated fleets. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1423) - [x] unit and integration tests for tokenbucket/smoothing - [x] e2e against a synthetic bursty workload - [x] updated Console dashboard panels and runbooks - [x] migration path for existing fleet configs (defaults preserve previous behavior). Testing: local and CI tests, dedicated canary fleet run for 48h with synthetic burst profile, monitored memory/CPU and queueing metrics. Observability: new metrics namespaced under redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.{utilization,guarantee,bucket_fill,queue_latency}. Backwards compatibility: all new config fields have sensible defaults; if throughput_guarantee is disabled, autoscaler reverts to prior behavior. Rollout plan: enable on 10% of fleets for 24h, validate p99 queue latency and error budget; increase to 50% then 100% over 3 days. Notes: this PR includes a small Helm chart bump for the dedicated controller config and a migration script to add a default throughput_guarantee block to fleets created before 2026-01-01.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid per-request locks in the admission path? Author: refactored admission to use a lock-free sampler and per-worker token caches, see tokenbucket.go; microbenchmarks show <2% overhead.

Wei Zhang: Need to ensure upgrade path doesn't change default throttling for existing fleets. Author: added migration script and ensured defaults map to previous behavior when throughput_guarantee.enabled=false.
Marta Ruiz: CI flake on e2e during first run (timing). Author: extended test timeouts and added retry logic; re-ran CI and all checks passed.
release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler: adds per-priority throughput guarantees, smoother burst controls, and enhanced utilization reporting. Configs default to previous behavior; enable via autoscaler.throughput_guarantee.enabled. See docs for migration and rollout guidance.
review_status: Approved by Wei Zhang and Marta Ruiz after 1 iteration; approver Liam O'Connor requested small perf clarifications satisfied in follow-up commit.
